dependency_graph.assessment: The graph resolves ciso8601 to pypi 2.4.1 (requires_python >=3.8) with zero forward dependency edges (direct or transitive) and 23 reverse dependents on PyPI (e.g. homeassistant, hass-nabucasa, faust-streaming, datacube). The Debian riscv64 binary python3-ciso8601 2.3.3 depends only on libc6 and python3. This agrees with the checkout: no install_requires, no native library; build/test-only deps (setuptools, wheel/build, pytz) are not modelled by the graph, so they were audited separately on PyPI. An empty result here reflects the absence of declared runtime edges, not missing data, because the project resolved successfully.

proposal.architecture_precedent: Dedicated native runner rows: ubuntu-24.04-arm/aarch64 and windows-11-arm/ARM64 (not a shared ubuntu-latest QEMU arch list). A riscv64 row on ubuntu-24.04-riscv follows this existing native-per-architecture topology.
proposal.build_backend: setuptools with setup.py Extension (module.c, timezone.c, isocalendar.c); no [build-system] table; no third-party native libraries. Build/test deps setuptools, wheel, build, pytz are pure-Python universal wheels on public PyPI (checked: pytz-2026.6-py2.py3-none-any, setuptools-84.2.1-py3-none-any, wheel-0.48.0-py3-none-any, build-1.6.1-py3-none-any); the RISE index has no entry for them and none is needed, so PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL/PIP_PREFER_BINARY are not required for this project.
proposal.contribution_rules: No CLA/DCO; fork-branch-PR flow; add a CHANGELOG entry; PEP 7 for C; no hand-written arch-specific code.
proposal.existing_riscv64_work: Open issue closeio/ciso8601#181 only; no upstream PR. Downstream RISE python-wheels#625 builds 2.3.3 cp312-cp314 riscv64 wheels.
proposal.fork_guards: None: no github.repository conditions in any workflow.

proposal.rationale: A concrete bounded CI/config patch can advance official riscv64 wheels: add a native ubuntu-24.04-riscv/riscv64 row to build-wheels.yml (matching the project's native-runner-per-arch topology used for aarch64 and Windows ARM64, not QEMU), skip the legacy cibuildwheel v3.4.1 step on that row because actions/setup-python has no riscv64 interpreter builds, list riscv64 in pyproject linux archs, and add a CHANGELOG line. The C code is portable (no assembly or arch dispatch, CONTRIBUTING forbids it), no native dependencies exist, closeio/cibuildwheel v4.3.5 supports riscv64 (manylinux_2_39 default image, cp39-cp315), and maintainers have merged similar rows (#151, #178). Risks: RISE runner app must be enabled by the closeio org; the runner needs python3 with venv/pip for the v4 action; cp38/pp riscv64 wheels will not be produced.

data.summary: ciso8601 2.4.1 (latest on PyPI, 80 files) ships no riscv64 wheel. The project is a single-phase-init pure C extension (module.c, timezone.c, isocalendar.c) built with setuptools via closeio/cibuildwheel, with no third-party native or Python build/runtime dependency beyond pure-Python setuptools/pytz. Upstream issue #181 requests riscv64 wheels; no upstream PR exists. Architecture precedent is dedicated native-runner rows (ubuntu-24.04-arm/aarch64, windows-11-arm/ARM64), not QEMU. Recommendation: develop a bounded configuration_integration patch adding an ubuntu-24.04-riscv/riscv64 matrix row to build-wheels.yml (skipping the legacy v3.4.1 step on that row because actions/setup-python has no riscv64 builds), adding riscv64 to pyproject linux archs, and a CHANGELOG entry. No sw-ecosystem report exists for this project.

PyPI 2.4.1 has no riscv64 wheel; no deps; precedent is native-runner rows (aarch64, win-arm64); issue #181 open; no sw-ecosystem report.
